tldr: Microsoft's record November Patch Tuesday (1,235+ flaws) included an actively exploited Outlook zero-day, while CISA flagged Cisco BroadWorks, Openwave and a critical Xen Orchestra auth-bypass as under live attack. Breach disclosures piled up at Maersk, Nitori (37.6M records), Baker Tilly and across MSPs via compromised ScreenConnect instances, alongside a GitHub supply-chain campaign that wiped its own logs after hijacking nearly 5,000 accounts.

emerging.title: Attackers weaponize open-source AI pentesting agents against AWS
emerging.description: Threat actors are self-hosting AntiFox, an open-source agentic AI red-teaming platform, on Alibaba Cloud to automate AWS credential theft and lateral movement — one of the first widely reported cases of offensive AI agent tooling weaponized live against production cloud environments. Unit 42 separately flagged the broader rise of AI-powered red-teaming tools (ARTEX and peers) being adopted by attackers.

items.title: Microsoft's record Patch Tuesday fixes 1,235+ flaws, including an exploited Outlook zero-day
items.description: November's update is Microsoft's largest ever, addressing over 60 critical bugs. CVE-2026-124194, an actively exploited Outlook flaw, may expose NTLMv2 hashes — patch immediately.

items.title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave flaws actively exploited despite available patches
items.description: CISA added Cisco BroadWorks (CVE-2026-20320, XXE) and Openwave Webtop (CVE-2026-111793) to its KEV catalog after confirming in-the-wild exploitation that can leak sensitive configuration data.

items.title: Critical Xen Orchestra auth-bypass flaw exploited to hijack VM hosts
items.description: Vates confirms active exploitation of an authentication bypass (VSA-2026-062) granting attackers global admin access and full takeover of XCP-ng virtualization hosts.

items.title: Maersk confirms breach as WhiteArmor ransomware demands $5 million
items.description: Shipping giant Maersk confirms attackers accessed a legacy system inherited from an acquisition and extracted data; WhiteArmor claims ~100GB stolen and demands bitcoin ransom. Maersk disputes some of the gang's claims.

items.title: Japanese furniture giant Nitori discloses breach of up to 37.6 million customer records
items.description: Nitori says unauthorized access discovered Nov 6 (breach occurred mid-to-late October) may have exposed names, addresses, phone numbers and emails; passwords and card data were not compromised.

items.title: Active ScreenConnect attacks breach MSPs, hitting dozens of organizations
items.description: Attackers used compromised ScreenConnect environments to push rogue remote-access clients to customer devices; ConnectWise disabled five third-party partner extensions in response.

items.title: 4,837 hijacked GitHub accounts ran a CI secret-stealer across 1,806+ repos, then wiped the logs
items.description: Aikido Security reports a mass supply-chain campaign using stolen GitHub credentials to plant secret-stealing workflows, followed by deliberate log deletion to hinder incident response.

items.title: eMudhra revokes 8 more CA certificates, widening a PKI private-key incident
items.description: The certificate authority revoked eight more intermediate CA certificates after finding additional improperly handled private keys it had previously declared unaffected — a trust-chain concern for any site relying on eMudhra-issued certs.

items.title: Russian Turla hackers breach government email servers to steal NATO/EU correspondence
items.description: ESET attributes a stealthy new Exchange-server toolkit ("Cereal") to Russia's FSB-linked Turla group, used against Romanian and Kazakh government mail servers configured to harvest NATO- and EU-addressed messages.

items.title: Baker Tilly notifies clients of data breach at a third-party provider
items.description: The accounting and advisory giant says a breach at a third-party vendor exposed personal information belonging to clients and their dependents.

action: Patch immediately where actively exploited: Microsoft Outlook (CVE-2026-124194), Cisco BroadWorks (CVE-2026-20320), Openwave Webtop (CVE-2026-111793), and Xen Orchestra (VSA-2026-062). MSPs and partners running ScreenConnect should audit for rogue client installs and unauthorized extensions now. Check for eMudhra-issued certificates against the latest revocation list. Any org using GitHub Actions should review workflows for unauthorized changes and rotate CI/CD secrets as a precaution given the active credential-harvesting campaign.
